features.name: Classed choropleths and symbol maps
features.summary: Maps: colorSpectrumBreaksMethod classifies a numeric colorBy into one colour class per colorSpectrum colour by Jenks natural breaks, quantile or equal width (or give colorSpectrumBreaks by hand) — fills are exact class colours that agree with a stepped legend (equal swatches, every class edge labelled; colorLegendSteps). showMapLabels draws region names that fit inside their region and never overlap (largest first, contrast-aware colour). Proportional-symbol maps: sizeBy a sample draws one bubble per region (world maps included) in mapBubbleColor, with a matching size legend. Insets: per-feature translate/scale via mapConfigFeatures.

features.summary: pushData appends new samples to a rendered chart and keeps a rolling window (streamWindow), recomputing fits and filters; dashboards subscribe panels to Server-Sent-Events streams without code.

features.name: Data wrangling
features.summary: A declarative dplyr/tidyr-style pipeline (dataPipeline), flexible group-by aggregation (aggregations) and formula-based calculated fields (calculatedFields, a safe evaluator, no eval).

features.name: Publishing tables (in-cell graphics)
features.summary: The data table (view:'table') draws per-column in-cell graphics with dataTableColRenderer: bars behind the values scaled to the column (zero baseline for negatives; summary and annotation rows excluded) and sparklines of each row across chosen columns (which may be hidden); heat colouring of cells via dataTableColored (toolbar colour toggle). dataTableColFormat takes sprintf strings or locale-aware number formats (comma, percent, dollar, compact, {locale, style, currency, decimals}). Graphics are re-applied on every render, so they follow virtual scrolling, sorting, filtering and pagination; the header menu toggles bars per column.

features.name: Themes
features.summary: 20+ built-in themes that control all non-data elements, including ggplot, bw, minimal, classic, Economist, Wall Street Journal, Tableau, Excel, Stata, solarized, dark and high-contrast.

features.name: UI theming (widget styles, dark mode, design tokens)
features.summary: The widgets around a chart (toolbar, menus, Customizer, data table, filters, dialogs) share one set of design tokens: dataUIStyle presets (all WCAG AA), light/dark/auto widgets that follow the chart theme, widgetsTheme or a page container's data-cx-ui-theme, and --cx-ui-* CSS variables to override any colour per page or per chart. In dark each preset keeps its own accent colour, lightened to stay readable (getDarkAccent; --cx-ui-dark-accent* to set it yourself), and colorful's per-item colours follow. Per-chart, so charts on one page can differ.

features.name: Locale-aware number formatting
features.summary: numberFormat (global) plus tooltipNumberFormat, legendNumberFormat, dataLabelNumberFormat and per-axis x/y/zAxisNumberFormat format displayed values with presets (comma, percent, dollar, euro, pound, yen, compact), sprintf strings, or an object {locale, style: decimal|percent|currency|compact, currency, decimals, grouping, prefix, suffix}. Intl.NumberFormat-backed with memoized formatter instances and a hand-written grouping fallback; axis width measurement follows the formatted strings. Default off keeps the legacy formatNumber output. An explicit *AxisTickFormat (sprintf) still wins per axis.

features.name: Structured chart footer
features.summary: Publication footer drawn on the canvas (included in PNG/SVG/PDF exports): notes (multiline), source with optional sourceUrl link, byline, and a 'Get the data' CSV download (showDataDownload), aligned with footerAlign. Clickable parts use a DOM overlay in the CanvasXpress wrapper. All off by default; the legacy citation keeps its exact position when used alone and moves above the footer block when both are set.

features.name: Editorial annotations and direct labels
features.summary: Callouts: decorations.marker anchors text to a data point (variable+sample) with a line, straight arrow or curved arrow connector, placed at plot-area fractions and draggable — drag writes the x/y fractions back into the config for reproducibility. Free text: decorations.text (scatter: data units or relative fractions; 1D: smp/catX + value). Direct labels: showLineEndLabels puts each series name at its line's end in the series color, hides the legend, nudges overlaps apart and reserves the right margin.

features.name: Editorial theme and responsive rules
features.summary: theme:'editorial' — publication look: light horizontal gridlines only, no panel box or tick marks, left-aligned title, muted grey text, restrained colourblind-safe PaulTol palette, white background. responsiveRules — width-based config overrides ([{maxWidth, minWidth, config}]) applied at render/resize (move or hide the legend, shrink fonts, thin labels at narrow widths) and reverted automatically when the width stops matching; the saved configuration is never mutated.

features.name: Screen-reader and keyboard accessibility
features.summary: Every chart gets a generated text summary (or the author's own alt text, a11yDescription, also written into SVG exports and as the tagged figure in PDF exports) and an off-screen data table kept in sync with the data, live-region announcements, a focusable canvas with arrow-key navigation between data points, keyboard-operable widgets, a visible focus outline, a high-contrast theme, and reduced motion when the OS requests it. WCAG 2.1 AA conformance report (VPAT-style) published.

features.name: Image and vector export
features.summary: Export to PNG (with high-resolution magnification), SVG, vector PDF (native writer: tagged with the alt text, the chart JSON attached like PNG/SVG and re-loadable), and the reproducible JSON config.

features.name: Reproducible specs (save and reload)
features.summary: A chart's full state serialises to a portable JSON config (getConfig) that reloads to the identical view, in JavaScript, R or Python.

features.name: Grammar of graphics and ggplot2 conversion
features.summary: Layered grammar-of-graphics rendering (geoms, stats, scales, coords, facets); R ggplot2 plots convert to CanvasXpress with close visual fidelity.

features.name: Language bindings and frameworks
features.summary: The same chart specification works in JavaScript, the R htmlwidget (Shiny, R Markdown, Quarto), Python (Jupyter, Dash, Streamlit, Flask) and Julia (CanvasXpress.jl: IJulia, Pluto, VS Code, Documenter), plus React, VS Code notebooks and Observable.

features.name: Dashboards and connectors
features.summary: canvasxpress-dashboards: linked multi-chart dashboards with shared filters, joins between sources, calculated fields on a source, a no-code builder, a data-first wizard (upload or paste data parsed by the CanvasXpress engine, a column check that flags bad cells, chart suggestions from the canvasxpress-mcp selector, one-click publish), share links and live sources, export of a dashboard (or a one-panel dashboard) as self-contained HTML, PNG or a print-ready PDF, publish & embed of a whole dashboard or a single chart (stable share URL republished in place on save, an auto-resizing iframe, a <cxd-embed> web component and a PNG fallback for RSS/email), an organisation brand lock (CXD_BRAND) enforced on saves and shared views, plus electronic records and signatures (immutable hash-chained version history with re-authenticated e-signatures, a Part 11 mapping) and scheduled data refresh; canvasxpress-connectors: SQL databases and cloud warehouses via SQLAlchemy, in-process DuckDB over Parquet/CSV, Google Sheets, Google Analytics, Salesforce and ServiceNow, with database pushdown (also in the browser) and no credential in the browser. Connector extras available: alphavantage, analytics, bigquery, databricks, duckdb, mssql, mysql, nasdaq, oracle, postgres, redshift, salesforce, servicenow, sheets, snowflake, stooq, teradata, yahoo.
